description: An online viewer that lets the public compare data on coal mines across Europe. The EEB project page says the database covers 145 coal mines (97 lignite, 39 hard coal and 11 coking coal), of which 120 operate, 7 are proposed and 19 are closed, retired or cancelled, occupying about 260,000 hectares and employing about 230,000 people, and links 76 groundwater bodies to the mines; over 36 per cent of mines lie in high water stress areas. The July 2023 methodology note says the mine list was built in 2021 by partners of the Beyond Fossil Fuels Coalition and correlated with Global Energy Monitor data, with fields for coal grade, calorific value, sulphur content, status, reserves, start year and life of mine, and water stress from the WRI Aqueduct atlas. The viewer and note are free to use online, but no free download of the table is offered on the pages read. Coverage is Europe including Turkey, Serbia and Kosovo. Caveats: the licence is not stated on the page read. For simulation it gives mine locations with water stress, to test how drought affects coal supply. A related catalogue record is the EU Industrial Emissions Portal.
